cards.a: NSF lets a router continue forwarding traffic while its control plane recovers during a supervisor/route-processor switchover. It works with SSO, and peers detect it via NSF capabilities, so forwarding continues while routing state is rebuilt.

cards.q: How do SSO and NSF work together?
cards.a: SSO keeps control-plane state, and NSF preserves forwarding while routing rebuilds gracefully, resulting in a seamless failover.

cards.q: How does graceful restart work during an NSF switchover?
cards.a: Capabilities are announced so the restart is peer unaware of any drop, routes are re-learned/reconstructed, and CEF keeps forwarding from the FIB, so convergence incurs no full flap.

cards.q: What role does an NSF-aware (helping) neighbor play?
cards.a: It detects the NSF-capable peer via hello/graceful signals, continues forwarding to the disabled peer, bridges the restart to avoid a flap, and holds state until final convergence after rebuild.
mode sso is the prerequisite, then under router ospf 1 use nsf (with nsf cisco for Cisco-specific or nsf ietf for the IETF standard), and for BGP use bgp graceful-restart under router bgp.

cards.q: How does NSF differ from BGP graceful restart (GR)?
cards.a: NSF applies to OSPF/EIGRP and uses a local curator with Cisco/IETF standards, while BGP GR applies to BGP and relies on the peer per RFC 4724. Both share the same zero-loss goal.

cards.q: What must be true for NSF to work?
cards.a: NSF requires SSO as its foundation, relies on CEF/FIB being independent of the control plane, is configured with nsf under the routing protocol or bgp graceful-restart, and peers must be NSF-aware to cooperate.
show ip ospf nsf verifies OSPF NSF, and show bgp neighbors with the Restart filter verifies BGP graceful restart.

cards.q: What is the forwarding behavior, base, and goal of NSF?
cards.a: Forwarding continues while the control plane rebuilds, SSO is its base, CEF/FIB is independent of the control plane, OSPF uses nsf and BGP uses graceful-restart, peers are aware, and the goal is zero loss.
